Norton, one of our new members, did very well to finish in the centre of the field and should feel bucked at beating such old campaigners as Joe Wilson and Jack Baker.
The 3 miles walk saw the field start off their time allowances and Joe Wilson, who went off the limit mark, set a good strong pace and was never headed.

The “B” team, of which we are equally proud, consisted of Joe Wilson, Dick Frazer, Fred Rolfe, Syd Spencer and Frank Jarvis, but, unfortunately, the latter blistered rather badly and was forced to retire.
Just before it is too late.—Congratulations to Jack Stirling-Wakely on winning the London to Brighton and Back Walk and to Joe Wilson for finishing the course in First Class Standard Time.
Jack led throughout and finished a comfortable winner from a big and classy field of notable distance walkers. Joe Wilson did extremely well to finish the course inside first-class standard time.
Our other " A " Team men, Dick Frazer, Fred Rolfe and Joe Wilson, all finished in the thirties. A most surprising race was walked by John Downs, a member who we have seen but little of.

Mention must be made of Joe and Percy Wilson, Harry Shields and Jack Goswell, who cycled all the way from Bath with our men, Jack Stirling-Wakely who walked about 65 miles with Fred Herring, Percy Wright and Bert Clayton who were willing helpers during the night in the wilds of Wiltshire, Frank Elso…
Our other walkers, Bernard Eglington, Joe Wilson, Percy Wilson, all gave a good account of themselves. The usual enthusiastic support was in evidence and much appreciated by the walkers.

Their peculiar way of awarding handicap prizes to the first 12 individuals instead of the teams, resulted in George Beecham taking 5th prize, George Checkley, 9th and Joe Wilson 12th, which was quite a good proportion.
To Joe Wilson, Gordon Doubleday, Len Demmon and Billie True and the ladies who came along to give their help and support ,we say thank you very much.

Our "A" team which also included George Beecham (11th) Fed Rolfe 25th, Doub, 33rd and Joe Wilson 34th, had six men home before any other club had completed their four.

At Croydon Norman Guilmant was 4thm George Beecham, very fit after his holiday 5th, Hugh McGreechan 7th, Harry Shields 20th and Bernard 23rd, with Fred Rolfe, Bert Stallardm Ron Fairman, Joe Wilson and George Oliver coming along behind.

It was a grand race with the back markers moving steadily through the field. With two laps to go Joe Wilson was in the lead only to be caught by no less than seven others, but off 680 yards returned 14.46.
Our "B" team was completed by Joe Wilson, George Webb and Dan Logan, who suffered from the cold. What a distance man Webb would make with regular training!
It was good to see Joe Wilson going so well after his accident and Bert East must have taken part in about twenty-five "Horwood Cup" races since the cup was instituted.

"Evergreen"Joe Wilson popped up yet again to win the Club Handicap from Will Belderson with Bob Barnes third. Our thanks are due to the officials judges and helpers who once again on a cold day enabled us to hold another Championship.

Ken Bailey seemed to be doing a steady training spin, while the extra miles suited Bernard Eglinton who shows steady improvement on each outing since his return from abroad. Joe Wilson made a strong effort to beat the handicapper once again, but this was not to be his day.

Consequently we were nowhere in the team Championship, although Bob Barnes walked most creditably, considering the absence of support, to finish 12th in 57:24. Gerry Cameron (24th in 60:06) carried off the third individual handicap and Joe Wilson took first Veterans' prize.

In our last issue I asked if there was a trophy available for presentation for our Annual Inter-School Relay and almost before the ink was dry PERCY WILSON, on behalf of himself and brother Joe, produced a fine shield which the Committee has been very pleased to accept.

Those two distance stalwarts Ray Hall and Pat Duncan did their best to screw each other throughout the race with Pat pulling away up the last hill " out of earshot ". Joe Wilson made a fool of the handicapper winning by over a minute and a half.
Two such men are the Wilson Brothers Joe and Percy, both members of the Walking Section. Sixty-one year old Joe, joined Belgrave in September 1939.
Our team of three (Jack Rutland, Tommy Green and Joe Wilson) tied with Leicester W. C. for third place, but our Midland friends took the awards on a lower time aggregate.
Joe and Percy Wilson brought up the rear in 104:24 and 105:52 respectively. The unofficial team result gave Belgrave the verdict over Vidarians 25 - 30.

In the same race Joe Wilson walked his usual sound race to become No. 164 in 21:04:46. Joe needs no introduction and is often at the roadside judging or helping with the feeding, or, indeed, giving his Club vest an airing.

We are saddened to hear that the Percy half of the stalwart Wilson brothers is seriously ill in Bolingbroke Hospital. Percy and Joe featured in our walking teams for many many years and I know that Joe will do all he can to keep the partnership going by conveying to Percy our best wishes for his recovery.

Eventually our lads finished in a procession with five consecutive placings from 18 to 22 and backed up by George Bentley, Joe Wilson and Joe Coleman, we succeeded in taking the Nijmegan Shield with our eight walkers in the first 48, an excellent performance on which all are to be congratulated.
